description:
(Summary from jobright.ai; the original posting may say more.)

The State of Missouri is hiring a Java developer to support the Department of Natural Resources. The role helps develop Java web applications and maintain existing applications through bug fixes and enhancements, working with agency staff and a collaborative Scrum team.
Java Developer developing web applications and supporting existing applications with bug fixes and small enhancements

Responsibilities:
• Help develop new Java web applications using the Scrum framework
• Assist with refining and estimating Product Backlog Items
• Contribute to writing and updating technical documentation
• Work with agency staff to address open tickets and requests
• Collaborate with the team and also complete tasks independently when needed
• Support existing applications by handling bug fixes and small enhancements

Requirements:
• Authorization to work in the United States
• will not sponsor applicants for work visas
• The role requires a foundational understanding of Java and a willingness to learn how to apply it to real‑world problem‑solving
• The applicant should be familiar with the Scrum framework and comfortable working in small, collaborative teams that may sometimes be dispersed
• They should be self‑motivated, eager to grow their skills, and maintain a positive attitude
• They should also demonstrate alignment with ITSD values: innovation, partnership, passion, respect, and integrity
• Java, J2EE (JSP, Servlet, EJB), DB2, SQL, HTML, CSS, MVC, Bootstrap, Web Application Security, JavaScript, Spring Boot, Struts
• Experience using Azure DevOps
• Strong written and verbal communication skills
• Strong analytical and problem‑solving skills
• Basic understanding of the Scrum framework
• Interest in process improvement
